definition: A tokenizer processes text to break it down into its constituent parts (tokens), which are often words or subwords, making the text more amenable to deep learning models.
details: A tokenizer processes text to break it down into its constituent parts (tokens), which are often words or subwords, making the text more amenable to deep learning models.

explainer.lead: A tokenizer breaks text into tokens, often words or subwords, so a model can process it. It is the first step of every language model pipeline and fixes what the model can see.

tiers.eli5: It's like chopping a sentence into puzzle pieces a computer can handle. The way you chop decides what the computer gets to work with.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick or train tokenizers before the model and must keep them matched to the deployment language mix. A pitfall is a tokenizer poorly suited to a language, which silently raises cost and lowers quality.
tiers.paperLevel: Maps a string to a sequence of tokens, then to numerical values. Probabilistic LLM tokenizers differ from compiler lexers, which use a lexical grammar and form the first phase of a compiler frontend.

explainer.example: In a compiler, a lexer converts source code into identifiers, operators and keywords; an LLM tokenizer converts text into tokens and then numbers.
